title.narrative: WE-GO Empowerment delle donne per opportunità green
WE-GO Women Empowerment for Green Opportunities

description.narrative: L’iniziativa viene proposta dal PAM in collaborazione con il Ministero Iracheno dell’Ambiente e Ministero dell’Agricoltura. Mira a contribuire al rafforzamento della resilienza in quattro Governatorati dell’Iraq centrale e meridionale (Ninive, Salah Al Din, Thi Qar e Bassora) e si articola in tre componenti: la creazione una governance partecipativa per le comunità locali rispetto al processo decisionale sulla resilienza, sulle capacità istituzionali di sostenere azioni nel settore agricolo maggiormente sostenibili e adatte agli effetti del cambiamento climatico ed infine sulla promozione di azioni concrete di economia green in ambito rurale. I partecipanti alle attività di progetto (3580 persone) saranno per il 95 % donne e l’obiettivo è di coinvolgere anche almeno un 30 % di beneficiari fra le persone con disabilità, per un totale di beneficiari diretti di 21.480 (partecipanti + famiglie). La strategia è in linea con i principi dell’Agroecologia e contribuisce al raggiungimento degli obiettivi fissati dalle Politiche Nazionali per lo Sviluppo e per la Sicurezza alimentare.

The initiative is proposed by WFP in collaboration with the Iraqi Ministry of Environment and Ministry of Agriculture. It aims to contribute to strengthening resilience in four Governorates of central and southern Iraq (Nineveh, Salah Al Din, Thi Qar and Basra) through three components: the creation of participatory governance mechanism for local communities with respect to decision-making on resilience, on the institutional capacity to support actions in the agricultural sector that are sustainable and adapted to the effects of climate change and finally on the promotion of concrete green economy actions in the rural areas. The participants in the project activities (3580 people) will be 95% women and the objective is to involve at least 30% of beneficiaries among people with disabilities, for a total of direct beneficiaries of 21,480 (participants + families). The strategy is in line with the principles of Agroecology and contributes to the objectives set by the National Policies for Development and Food Security.

tag.narrative: Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls

By 2030, build the resilience of the poor and those in vulnerable situations and reduce their exposure and vulnerability to climate-related extreme events and other economic, social and environmental shocks and disasters

By 2030, double the agricultural productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers, in particular women, indigenous peoples, family farmers, pastoralists and fishers, including through secure and equal access to land, other productive resources and inputs, knowledge, financial services, markets and opportunities for value addition and non-farm employment

By 2030, ensure sustainable food production systems and implement resilient agricultural practices that increase productivity and production, that help maintain ecosystems, that strengthen capacity for adaptation to climate change, extreme weather, drought, flooding and other disasters and that progressively improve land and soil quality
End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture
End poverty in all its forms everywhere
Ensure women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making in political, economic and public life
Improve education, awareness-raising and human and institutional capacity on climate change mitigation, adaptation, impact reduction and early warning
Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts
